warmup.name: Torso Rotations
warmup.explanation:
Starting Position:
Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart. You can either place your hands on your hips or bend your arms 90 degrees at your sides. Keep your back straight and your core gently engaged. 

Rotation: 
Slowly rotate your upper body (torso and shoulders) to one side as far as is comfortable. Allow the foot on the opposite side to pivot slightly on the ball of the foot to avoid excessive twisting in the knee and lower back. 

Reverse: 
Return to the starting center position in a controlled manner. 

Opposite Side: 
Repeat the rotation to the other side, pivoting the opposite foot. Form Tips: The movement should be slow and controlled, focusing on the rotation coming from your trunk, not just swinging your arms. Keep your head relatively aligned with your torso.

warmup.name: Arm Circles
warmup.explanation:
Starting Position: 
Stand upright with your feet about shoulder-width apart. Extend both arms straight out to your sides at shoulder height, forming a T shape with your body.

Forward Circles: 
Begin by rotating both arms forward simultaneously in small, controlled circular motions. 

Reverse Direction: 
Once you complete the desired time or repetitions, immediately reverse the direction and rotate your arms backward. 

 Form Tips: 
Keep your arms straight and your core stable to prevent your back from arching or swaying. The movement should be smooth and controlled, originating from the shoulder joint.

warmup.name: Step Jacks
warmup.explanation:
Starting Position: 
Stand upright with your feet together and your arms resting at your sides.

Step Out and Up: 
Step your right foot out wide to the side. Simultaneously, swing both arms out to the sides and up over your head until your hands nearly touch (like the top of a Jumping Jack).

Return to Center:
Step your right foot back to meet your left foot. At the same time, bring both arms back down to your sides in a controlled motion.

Alternate Sides: 
Repeat the entire movement on the opposite side, stepping out with your left foot and raising your arms overhead.

Flow: 
Continue alternating sides, keeping a steady, fluid rhythm. Maintain good posture and keep your core engaged throughout the movement.

warmup.name: High Knees
warmup.explanation:
Starting Position: 
Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your arms bent at 90 degrees, held close to your sides, as if you were about to run.

The Movement: 
Begin walking in place. As you do, drive one knee up toward your chest (aiming for hip level or a 90-degree bend) and quickly return that foot to the ground.

Alternate and Pump: 
Immediately switch legs, driving the opposite knee up. Maintain a quick, continuous, and rhythmic alternating motion.

Arm Action: 
Keep your core engaged and pump your arms vigorously in coordination with the opposite leg, just as you would while sprinting.

Form Tips: 
Land softly on the balls of your feet to reduce impact. Keep your back straight, chest up, and avoid leaning backward. To make it a lower-impact exercise, you can start with a slow, controlled marching motion.

liedown.name: Glute Bridges
liedown.explanation:
Starting Position: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground. Your feet should be hip-width apart and positioned so that your fingertips can just graze your heels. Rest your arms straight by your sides, palms flat on the floor.

Engage and Lift: Squeeze your glutes (buttocks) and brace your core (imagine pulling your belly button toward your spine). Press through your heels and drive your hips upward off the floor.

Top Position: Continue lifting until your body forms a straight, diagonal line from your shoulders to your knees. Avoid over-arching your lower back; the movement should come from the hip extension, powered by your glutes.

Hold and Lower: Squeeze your glutes tightly at the top of the movement for a few seconds hold. Then, slowly and with control, lower your hips back down to the starting position on the floor.

Repeat: Complete the desired number of repetitions, maintaining core engagement throughout the entire set.

liedown.name: Flutter Kicks
liedown.explanation:
Starting Position: Lie on your back on the floor, with your legs extended straight out. 

Hand Position (Modification): For beginners or those with lower back strain, place your hands palms-down underneath your glutes/hips for support. For a more challenging version, keep your arms straight by your sides or behind your head. 

Engage Core: Crucially, press your entire lower back flat into the floor. Imagine pulling your belly button down to your spine. You must maintain this flat back throughout the exercise. 

Lift the Legs: Keeping your legs straight (or with a very slight bend in the knee if necessary), lift both feet about 10 cm off the ground. 

Optional Challenge: For greater intensity, you can lift your head, neck, and shoulders slightly off the ground (a hollow body position), keeping your chin tucked. 

The Flutter: Keeping your legs straight, begin to quickly and alternately move your legs up and down in a small, controlled range of motion, like a flutter kick in swimming. The movement should come from the hip joint, with the knees remaining mostly straight. Keep the kicks small and controlled. Avoid large, swinging motions that cause your lower back to lift off the floor. 

Breathing and Control: Breathe steadily and consistently. Continue the flutter motion for the set time

liedown.name: Reverse Snow Angels
liedown.explanation:
Starting Position (Prone): Lie face-down on a mat with your legs extended straight. Extend your arms straight out overhead, palms facing down (or thumbs pointing up). 

Core Engagement: Gently engage your glutes and core to prevent over-arching in your lower back. 

The Lift (Superman Hold): Keeping your neck neutral (gazing at the floor), gently lift your head, chest, and arms a few cm off the floor. You can also lift your feet slightly if you can maintain the lower back stability. The key is maintaining this elevated position throughout the entire movement. 

The Sweep (The Angel): Keeping your arms straight, slowly and with control, sweep them out wide in a semicircular arc toward your hips. 

As your arms sweep down: Your hands will rotate so your palms face the ceiling as they reach your sides/hips. You should be actively squeezing your shoulder blades together (scapular retraction) and down toward your spine. Do not let your arms touch the ground during the sweep. 

The Return: Slowly and with control, reverse the movement, sweeping your arms back overhead to the starting position. Your palms will rotate back to face the floor (or thumbs up) as they reach the top. Maintain the lift and the tension in your upper back throughout the entire repetition. 

Key Focus Points: Control is King: Perform the movement slowly and deliberately—do not rely on momentum. This is about building muscle control and endurance. 
Squeeze the Back: The main focus is the squeeze of the shoulder blades together when your hands are near your hips. 
Neutral Spine: Keep your chin slightly tucked and your gaze on the floor to maintain a neutral alignment between your head and spine. Avoid craning your neck.

arms.name: Push-ups
arms.explanation:
Starting Position (High Plank): Start on your hands and knees. Place your hands on the floor slightly wider than your shoulders, with your fingers pointing forward. Extend your legs straight behind you, balancing on your toes. Your body should form one straight line from your head to your heels.

Engage Core: Brace your core and squeeze your glutes tightly to prevent your hips from sagging or rising. Keep your neck neutral by looking down at the floor.

Lower Down: Inhale and slowly bend your elbows, lowering your chest toward the floor. Keep your elbows tucked in at a 45-degree angle from your body (avoid letting them flare out to the sides).

Push Up: Exhale and powerfully push through your palms to straighten your arms, returning to the high plank starting position. Maintain a straight body line throughout the entire movement.

Repeat: Complete the desired number of repetitions, focusing on a slow, controlled descent and a powerful push up.

arms.name: Pike Push-ups
arms.explanation:
Starting Position (Pike/Inverted V): Keep your legs and arms as straight as possible. Your body should form an inverted V shape. If your hamstrings are tight, a slight bend in the knees is acceptable, or you can stand on your toes. 

Hand Placement: Your hands should be flat on the floor, roughly shoulder-width apart (or slightly wider/turned out if your wrists are sensitive). 

Engage CoreThe Lean (Setup): Before you start the push-up, you must shift your weight. Lean your shoulders forward so they are stacked almost directly over your wrists (or even slightly in front of them). 

Key Cue: Your body (from hips to hands) should be in a straight diagonal line. This is crucial for proper shoulder loading. 

The Descent (Lowering): Keeping your body tight and your hips elevated, slowly bend your elbows and lower your head toward the floor. 

Direction of Movement: Your head should aim for a spot in front of your hands, essentially tracing a path forward and down. Do not lower your head straight down between your hands (this flares your elbows and reduces shoulder emphasis).Keep your elbows tucked to about a 45-degree angle relative to your body.Lower until the top of your head gently touches the ground, or as far as you comfortably can.

The Ascent (Pushing): Explosively push through your hands and press your body back up to the starting inverted V position. Finish the rep by pushing your shoulders back up and forward to achieve the active shoulder position directly over your hands again.

arms.name: Down Under
arms.explanation:
Starting Position (Downward Dog): Begin on your hands and feet. Push your hips high and back, forming an inverted 'V' shape with your body. Your hands should be slightly wider than shoulder-width, fingers spread, and your head should be between your arms. This is the Downward Dog position.

The Dive (The Down Under): Bend your elbows and, in a smooth, continuous, sweeping motion, lower your chest in an arc towards the floor, as if you are diving under a low bar. Your head should sweep down toward the ground, then forward past your hands.

The Push-Up and Arch (The Cobra): As your chest clears the floor, straighten your arms to lift your torso up, arching your back and lifting your head and chest up and forward. Your hips should be near, but not resting on the floor, with the tops of your feet flat or toes tucked (depending on your preference). This resembles the Cobra or Upward-Facing Dog pose.

The Return: From the arched position, use your core and shoulder strength to lift your hips back up and back, reversing the movement to return to the Downward Dog starting position. The movement should be fluid, completing a full cycle of contraction and extension.

arms.name: Self-arm wrestling
arms.explanation:
Starting Position: Stand and lock hands (one will act as your 'opponent').

Grip: Your dominant hand should mimic an arm wrestling grip. Your non-dominant hand wraps around it to provide resistance. Focus on a strong, unyielding grip with your dominant hand.

Apply Tension (The 'Wrestle'): Engage the muscles of your dominant arm (forearm, bicep, and shoulder) as if you are trying to beat an opponent. At the same time, use your non-dominant arm to resist the movement, creating a static, pushing tension (like a max-effort hold).

Hold: Hold this isometric contraction for a set period, maintaining maximum tension and fighting for control. Do not allow either arm to move.

Release and Switch: Slowly release the tension and rest briefly. After completing the hold with your dominant arm, switch hands and repeat the process. 

Note: To target different angles of the arm wrestling motion (e.g., pronation or 'toproll'), you can adjust your grip to focus on turning your wrist down or up against your own resistance.

arms.name: Tricep Dips
arms.explanation:
Starting Position: Sit on the edge of a stable bench, box, or sturdy chair. Place your hands shoulder-width apart, gripping the edge with your fingers pointing forward (towards your feet) or slightly out to the sides. 

Setup: Keeping your back straight, slide your hips forward off the bench. Your weight should be supported by your hands and your feet. Keep your legs straight or bent at a 90-degree angle (bent knees make the exercise easier).

The Descent (Dip): Keeping your torso upright and your back close to the bench, slowly bend your elbows, lowering your body toward the floor. Ensure your elbows point straight back behind you, not flaring out to the sides.

The Bottom: Continue lowering until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor, forming a 90-degree angle at the elbow, or as low as your shoulder comfort allows. Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.

The Ascent (Push-Up): Press firmly through your palms, engaging your triceps to straighten your arms and push your body back up to the starting position. Stop just short of locking your elbows to maintain tension on the triceps. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

core.name: Rotating Plank
core.explanation:
Starting Position (Plank): Begin in a standard high or low plank position: hands directly under your shoulders, body in a straight line from head to heels. Your feet should be placed slightly wider than hip-width apart for better stability.

2. First Rotation (Right Arm Up): Shift your weight onto your left arm and the outside edge of your left foot. Engage your core as you pivot your body and rotate to your right. Lift your right arm straight up toward the ceiling. Your body should form a T shape, and your hips should be stacked (one directly above the other).

Return to Center: Hold the side plank briefly, then slowly rotate back down, bringing your right hand back to the floor to return to the original plank position.

Second Rotation (Left Arm Up): Shift your weight onto your right arm and the outside edge of your right foot. Engage your core as you pivot and rotate to your left. Lift your left arm straight up toward the ceiling.

Alternating Repetition: Return the left hand to the floor to return to the plank position. Continue to alternate the rotation from side to side for the desired number of repetitions or time.

core.name: Inchworms
core.explanation:
Starting Position: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your core engaged. Keep your legs as straight as possible without locking your knees.

Hinge and Reach: Hinge at your hips and bend down to place your hands on the floor a few inches in front of your feet. Bend your knees slightly if your hamstrings are too tight to reach the floor.

Walk Out: Slowly walk your hands forward, one at a time (like an inchworm), keeping your core tight and your back flat. Continue walking your hands until your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels, ending in a high plank position (hands directly under your shoulders).

Walk Back: Pause in the plank for a moment. Now, keeping your hands planted, begin to walk your hands backs in small steps, one at a time. Keep your legs as straight as you comfortably can to feel a stretch in your hamstrings and calves. Your hips will lift toward the ceiling as your hands get closer to your feet.

Return to Start: Continue walking your hands back until you can no longer keep your legs straight (or they are as close to your feet as possible). From this 'pike' position, stand back up by straightening your torso. That completes one repetition. Repeat the entire cycle: Hands Out, Hands In.

core.name: Standing bicycle crunch (Alternating)
core.explanation:
Starting Position: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart and a soft bend in your knees. Place your hands lightly behind your head, flaring your elbows out wide. Engage your core by keeping your chest up and a slight brace in your abdomen. 

First Rep (Twist Right): Exhale as you simultaneously lift your right knee up toward your chest and twist your torso to bring your left elbow toward that knee. Focus on crunching your side muscles (obliques) to initiate the movement, maintaining your balance on your standing leg. 

Return to Center: Inhale as you smoothly lower your right foot back to the floor and return your torso to the upright starting position. 

Second Rep (Twist Left): Exhale as you immediately repeat the movement on the opposite side: lift your left knee up and twist your torso to bring your right elbow toward that knee. 

Alternating Repetition: Continue to alternate sides in a controlled, rhythmic motion, emphasizing the crunch and twist in your core rather than just pulling your leg or leaning forward.

core.name: Ab-Rolls
core.explanation:
Starting Position: Kneel on a mat with your knees directly under your hips (or slightly behind them for more intensity). Place the ab wheel on the floor directly under your shoulders. Grip the handles with straight arms. Tuck your pelvis slightly and brace your core hard, keeping your back flat—you should look like a straight line from your head to your knees. 

The Rollout (Eccentric Phase): Slowly and with deliberate control, push the wheel forward. Maintain the tight, braced core position, focusing on preventing your lower back from arching (anti-extension). Your arms should remain straight, and your hips should move with your shoulders. 

The End Point: Roll out only as far as you can maintain the perfect, flat-back position. Stop immediately if you feel your lower back begin to sag or arch. 

The Return (Concentric Phase): Exhale and intensely squeeze your abs and lats to pull the wheel back to the starting position. The force should come from your core, reeling your body in, not from a push with your hips or arms. 

Repetition: Reset your core brace and repeat the movement, focusing on slow control, especially during the rollout phase.

core.name: Dog-bird
core.explanation:
Starting Position (Tabletop): Begin on all fours in a tabletop position. Your knees should be directly under your hips and your hands directly under your shoulders, creating a stable box shape. Look down at the floor to keep your neck in line with your spine. Engage your abs slightly to brace your core and establish a neutral spine (flat back). 

The Extension: Exhale and slowly extend one arm straight out in front (palm facing inward) and the opposite leg straight out behind you. Both limbs should stop at hip/shoulder height, forming a straight, parallel line with your torso. 

Hold and Stabilize: The critical part of the movement is the pause. Hold the extended position for a few seconds, focusing on keeping your hips and shoulders square to the floor (imagine balancing a glass of water on your lower back). Do not allow your lower back to arch or your torso to rotate. Try to reach as far forward and backwards as possible. 

The Return: Inhale as you slowly and with control return the extended arm and leg back to the tabletop starting position. 

Alternating Repetition: Immediately repeat the movement on the opposite side (the other arm and leg). Continue to alternate sides smoothly, maintaining a braced core throughout the entire set.

core.name: Push-up to Plank
core.explanation:
Starting Position (High Plank): Begin in a high plank position. Your hands should be placed directly beneath your shoulders, arms straight, and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. Engage your core and squeeze your glutes.

Lower Down to Forearm Plank: Lead with one arm (e.g., the right arm). Lower your right forearm to the ground where your hand was, then immediately follow with your left forearm, so you are now in a standard forearm plank position. Keep your core braced to prevent your hips from swaying or tilting.

Push Up to High Plank: Lead with the same arm (the right arm). Place your right hand back on the ground, pressing up to straighten the arm. Immediately follow with your left hand, returning to the high plank starting position.

Repeat and Alternate: Continue the movement, but on the next repetition, alternate the leading arm. For instance, go down left-right and come up left-right. The goal is to perform the exercise with minimal hip rotation or movement.

Pacing: Focus on a slow, controlled movement rather than speed. Maintaining a rigid, straight spine and square hips is more important than the number of reps.

legs.name: Squats
legs.explanation:
Starting Position: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder-width apart, or slightly wider—whatever feels most stable and natural for your body. Your toes should be pointed slightly outward (about 10 to 30 degrees). Keep your chest up and your core braced. 

The Descent (Lowering Phase): Initiate the movement by simultaneously pushing your hips back and bending your knees, as if you are trying to sit down in a chair far behind you. As you lower, actively push your knees out so they track in line with your feet/toes. Keep your chest up and your spine neutral—your torso will naturally lean forward, but avoid rounding your lower back. 

The Depth: Continue lowering until your hip crease drops below your knees (parallel or deeper), or as far down as you can comfortably go without your lower back rounding or your heels lifting off the floor. Your weight should remain balanced over the middle of your feet. It's important to ensure that your knees never exceed your toes. 

The Ascent (Lifting Phase): Drive forcefully through your entire foot (especially the heels and outside edges) to push yourself back up to the starting position. Focus on squeezing your glutes to drive your hips forward as you fully stand up. 

Repetition: Return to the tall, standing position, maintain your core tension, and immediately begin the next repetition.

legs.name: Stationary Lunges
legs.explanation:
Starting Position: Start kneeling on the ground (a mat or cushion is helpful for comfort). Place one foot forward, creating two 90 degree angles: one at the front knee and one at the back knee. Your feet should be hip-width apart for better stability. Core is tight and your torso is straight and tall.

The Ascent (Lifting Phase): Drive your weight through the front foot and the toes of the back foot to lift your body straight up until your front leg is fully extended (or mostly straight). Keep your torso vertical and your hips squared forward. 

The Top Position: Pause briefly at the top in a tall split-stance standing position. 

The Descent (Lowering Phase): Slowly and with control, lower your body straight back down until your back knee almost touches the ground (or returns to the starting position). Control the weight all the way down, do not let gravity drop you. 

Repetition: You can either pause briefly on the ground (to reset your balance) or immediately drive back up for the next rep. Complete all reps on this side before switching legs.

legs.name: Calf Raises
legs.explanation:
Starting Position: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart and your toes pointing straight ahead. If you need balance, lightly rest your hands on a wall, chair back, or sturdy object. 

The Ascent (Lifting Phase): Keeping your legs straight (but without locking your knees), slowly press through the balls of your feet to raise your heels off the floor. Continue rising until you are as high up on your toes as possible. Pause and squeeze the calf muscles hard at the very top of the movement. 

The Top Position: You should be on your tiptoes, feeling a strong contraction in the back of your lower leg. Avoid rolling your ankles outward or inward. 

The Descent (Lowering Phase): Slowly and with control, lower your heels back down to the starting position. Take your time on the way down (this is the most effective part of the exercise for muscle growth). 

Repetition: Immediately begin the next repetition without resting your weight on your heels at the bottom. The goal is to keep tension on the calf muscles throughout the set.

legs.name: Single Leg Deadlift
legs.explanation:
Starting Position: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and a soft bend in your knees. Maintain a neutral spine and brace your core.

First Rep (Right Leg Standing): Shift your weight onto your right leg (the standing leg). Slowly begin to hinge at the right hip, pushing your hips backward. As your torso lowers toward the ground, simultaneously lift and extend your left leg straight back. Your body should form a straight line from your head to your left heel. Keep your hips square (level and facing the floor) and go only as low as you can without rounding your back or losing balance.

Return to Center: Drive through the heel of your right leg to return to a standing position, bringing your left foot back to meet your right.

Second Rep (Left Leg Standing): Shift your weight onto your left leg. Hinge at the left hip, lifting and extending your right leg straight back until your torso and right leg are parallel to the floor (or your maximum range). Maintain a tight core and square hips.

Alternating Repetition: Drive through the heel of your left leg to return to the standing position. Continue to alternate the standing leg with each repetition, moving with control and focus.

flow.name: Crab Crawl
flow.explanation:
Starting Position: Sit on the floor with your knees bent, feet flat on the ground (about hip-width apart). Place your hands on the floor a few centimeters behind your hips, with your fingers pointing directly away from your body (i.e., pointing backward). 

The Lift: Press firmly into your hands and feet to lift your hips and torso off the ground. 

Hip Height: Keep your hips slightly lifted off the ground the entire time. The key is to keep tension in your glutes and core so you are not resting your weight fully on your lower back. 

Head/Neck: Keep your head in a neutral position, looking up at the ceiling or straight ahead. 

The Crawl (Movement): Begin to walk forward or backward by moving an opposite arm and leg together (e.g., right hand and left foot, then left hand and right foot). 

Forward Crawl (Backward Direction): To move your body forward, you will be moving your limbs backward. Lead with the hand and the foot of the opposite side, taking small, controlled steps. 

Backward Crawl (Forward Direction): To move your body backward, you will be moving your limbs forward. 

Maintaining Form: Focus on keeping the hips suspended and elevated off the floor. Do not let your glutes drag. The movement should be deliberate and controlled, not a frantic shuffle.

flow.name: Bear Crawl
flow.explanation:
Starting Position (All Fours): Start on your hands and knees. Place your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips. Look down at the floor to keep your neck neutral. 

The Lift: Tuck your toes, engage your core, and lift your knees just a few centimeters off the ground. Your back should be flat and parallel to the floor—imagine balancing a glass of water on your lower back. This is your loaded starting position. 

The Crawl (Movement): Move forward by simultaneously stepping with your right hand and left foot, taking small, controlled steps. 

Opposite Coordination: Immediately follow by stepping with your left hand and right foot. 

Crucial Tip: Maintain this contralateral (opposite arm and leg) pattern throughout the movement. 

Maintaining Form: The key is to keep your back flat, your hips low, and minimize any side-to-side rotation or excessive bouncing of the hips. Your knees must remain hovering just above the ground the entire time.

flow.name: Side Kick Through
flow.explanation:
Starting Position (All Fours): Get into the Bear Crawl starting position (hands under shoulders, knees under hips). Lift your knees just a few centimeters off the ground. This is your Active Beast hold. 

Unload and Pivot: To execute a Right Side Kick Through, you will first lift (unload) the right hand and the left foot (the contralateral limbs). Simultaneously, you will pivot on the ball of your right foot and your left hand. 

The Kick Through: Sweep your left leg (the unloaded leg) underneath your body and across to the right side, fully extending it straight. The heel should kick through to the side. As you kick through, your right foot (the base foot) should rotate outward to a 90-degree angle, dropping the heel to the floor to create a stable base. Your hips will naturally drop low to the ground. Your right hand (the unloaded hand) will move away from the floor and can reach back toward the kicking foot or extend up/out for balance. 

The Return (Reverse the Movement): Lift the extended leg and bring it back through the space you created. Simultaneously, place the right hand back down under the shoulder and pivot back onto the ball of your right foot. You should land softly back in the Active Beast (bear crawl) position, ready to repeat on the same side or transition to the other side. 

Key Focus Points Opposites Move: Remember, the foot you lift is the leg that kicks through, and the hand you lift is the arm that sweeps off the ground. They are contralateral to the movement side (e.g., Left Kick Through uses Right Hand/Left Foot lift). 
Controlled Rotation: The power of the movement comes from the controlled rotation of your core and hips. Avoid just flopping into the position. 
Shoulder Stack: The grounded hand's shoulder must remain strong, stable, and stacked directly.

flow.name: Front Kick Through
flow.explanation:
Starting Position (All Fours): Start in a bear crawl position: hands under shoulders, knees lifted a few centimeters off the ground. 

The Front Step (Load): To initiate a Left Front Kick Through, step your right foot forward and plant it on the outside of your right hand. Simultaneously, lift your right hand off the ground (creating space for the foot) and shift your weight slightly back onto your rear leg. The front knee should be bent (like a deep lunge), your back knee still hovers, and your left hand is in contact with the ground. 

The Kick Through: Using the momentum and stability from your grounded left hand and right foot, forcefully swing your left leg (the backward leg) forward and kick it through the space under your torso, extending it straight infront of you and slightly upward. As the left leg kicks through, you will be balancing entirely on your left hand and the ball of your right foot. Your hips will be high. 

The Return (Recoil): Bring the kicking left leg back to land softly near its starting Front Step position. Simultaneously, plant your right hand back down. 
Repeat but lead with the other leg. 

If this proves too difficult, try just stepping forward and back until you are ready to kick your leg through the space under your torso.
